notes: Eclipse Loop 1.6.2 The tempo track actually re-times the song The tempo lane in ARRANGE was cosmetic: dropping a tempo point moved the metronome and the BPM readout while the audio kept its original spacing. Now a tempo point moves everything after it — audio clips, MIDI notes, the A–B loop region, clip fades and frozen tracks. Write a half-time drop, a build into the chorus, or a ritardando on the last bar. - A point placed at bar 5 leaves bars 1–4 at the project tempo. It used to report and apply its BPM from the very start of the song. - The playhead, the ruler click-seek, Jump to bar, clip follow-actions and the TIME readout all use the same tempo mapping as playback, so the cursor and the clock stay locked to what you hear. - Songs with no tempo points are completely unchanged — timing is identical to previous versions, so existing projects play exactly as before. Warp clips to the grid Right-click any audio clip in ARRANGE → Warp clip to fit slot. The clip is time-stretched — pitch-preserved, not repitched — to fill its slot exactly, so a loop recorded at another tempo sits on this song's grid without chopping. Warped clips follow tempo points too, and carry a WARP badge so you can see which ones are stretched. Warp is applied identically in playback, Bounce Song, stem export and freeze — what you hear is what you export. Off by default; applies to every selected clip at once. Crash recovery that keeps your sound The autosave saved your project every 30 seconds but the audio only on a clean quit — so a crash, a force-quit, or the app being updated underneath you reopened the session with every clip in place and silence coming out. - Audio now autosaves on the same 30-second cadence, encoded on a background thread so nothing stutters, and written safely enough that being killed mid-write cannot leave a broken file. - If Eclipse Loop closes without quitting, the next launch asks whether to recover. A normal quit still reopens silently, with no prompt to dismiss. - Start fresh moves the old session into a dated recovered-… folder instead of discarding it, so changing your mind is free. Mixer and arranger fixes - Arranger faders were applied twice — squared — so a track set to −6 dB actually played at −12, and pan ran through two different laws. There is now a single track gain stage. Existing arranger tracks below unity will play louder than before; that is the fix landing. - Mute and Solo now act as one gate across both engines. A track's audio can leave through the arranger or the step sequencer, and M/S only ever silenced one of them — so mute did not always mute, and soloing an arranger track never silenced the loop or the SEQ rows. - Freeze captures the track's content, not its fader. Freezing used to bake the fader into the rendered file (doubling it on playback) and left the fader dead on a frozen track. - Bounce and stem export were computing clip positions at a single BPM of their own, so an export could not match what you just listened to. Both now share the arranger's timing.
